questions.question: On this day in 1885, the Russian cargo ship Dmitry ran aground at Whitby, later inspiring an iconic arrival scene in which Gothic horror novel?
questions.explanation: The wreck of the Dmitry in Whitby harbour provided inspiration for Count Dracula's dramatic arrival on English shores in Bram Stoker's classic work.
questions.context:
On this day in 1885: The Russian ship Dmitry ran aground in Whitby, an incident that inspired the arrival of Count Dracula to England in Bram Stoker's 1897 novel (cover pictured).
Russian ship Dmitry (Cargo ship wrecked at England in 1885): Dmitry was a Russian cargo ship that was wrecked at Whitby, England, in 1885. The vessel had been travelling from Antwerp, Belgium, to Newcastle upon Tyne, England, when she sought safe harbour in Whitby during a gale on 24 October.

questions.question: Which stop-motion studio produced the 2026 dark fantasy animated film Wildwood?
questions.explanation: Wildwood is an American stop-motion fantasy film produced by Laika and directed by Travis Knight.
questions.context: Wildwood (film) (2026 American film): Wildwood is a 2026 American stop-motion adult animated epic dark fantasy film directed by Travis Knight and written by Chris Butler, based on the 2011 novel by Colin Meloy and Carson Ellis. Produced by Laika, the film stars Carey Mulligan, Peyton Elizabeth Lee, Jacob Tremblay, Richard E. Grant, Awkwafina, Amandla Stenberg, Tom Waits, Charlie Day, Blythe Danner, Arthur Knight, Angela Bassett, and Mahershala Ali.

questions.question: Who hosts the second series of the BBC One reality game show The Celebrity Traitors?
questions.explanation: Claudia Winkleman serves as the presenter for the ten-episode celebrity edition of the programme.
questions.context: The Celebrity Traitors series 2 (2026 series of The Celebrity Traitors): The second series of The Celebrity Traitors began airing on BBC One on 1 October 2026, with Claudia Winkleman presenting the ten-episode series. The companion show The Celebrity Traitors: Uncloaked has also returned, hosted by Ed Gamble. In the series, 21 celebrities compete to win up to £100,000 for their chosen charities.

questions.question: What primary method did Elizabeth Holmes claim would revolutionise blood testing when promoting her company Theranos?
options: Analysing saliva samples instead of venous draws
Detecting pathogens via continuous skin patches
Testing very small volumes such as from a fingerprick
Using optical scanning without breaking the skin
questions.explanation: Theranos claimed to have created innovative technology requiring merely tiny amounts of blood taken from a simple fingerprick.
questions.context: Elizabeth Holmes (American businesswoman and convicted felon (born 1984)): Elizabeth Anne Holmes is an American businesswoman convicted of fraud in connection with her health technology company Theranos. Holmes founded Theranos in 2003, and its valuation soared in the early 2010s after it claimed to have revolutionized blood testing by developing methods that needed only very small volumes of blood, such as from a fingerprick.

questions.question: In which American state did Ilhan Omar serve as a state representative from 2017 to 2019 before entering the U.S. Congress?
questions.explanation: Ilhan Omar represented a section of Minneapolis in the Minnesota House of Representatives prior to her election to Congress.
questions.context: Ilhan Omar (American politician (born 1982)): Ilhan Abdullahi Omar is an American politician serving as the U.S. representative for Minnesota's 5th congressional district since 2019. The district includes all of Minneapolis and some of its first-ring suburbs. From 2017 to 2019, Omar served in the Minnesota House of Representatives, representing part of Minneapolis. She is a member of the Democratic Party.
